title: Preventing P-Trap Siphonage and Sewer Gas Leaks
description: A P-trap relies on a standing water seal inside its dip to block sewer gases from entering living spaces. However, if a P-trap is improperly vented or connected with an unvented vertical drop—creating an S-trap configuration—the discharging water creates a suction effect. This self-siphoning action pulls the standing water seal right out of the trap as the flow finishes. To keep the trap seal intact, the trap arm must extend horizontally to a proper vent connection before dropping vertically. Correct venting equalizes atmospheric pressure, preventing siphonage and ensuring harmful sewer odors stay inside the drainage system.

Preventing P-Trap Siphonage and Sewer Gas Leaks

A P-trap relies on a standing water seal inside its dip to block sewer gases from entering living spaces. However, if a P-trap is improperly vented or connected with an unvented vertical drop—creating an S-trap configuration—the discharging water creates a suction effect. This self-siphoning action pulls the standing water seal right out of the trap as the flow finishes. To keep the trap seal intact, the trap arm must extend horizontally to a proper vent connection before dropping vertically. Correct venting equalizes atmospheric pressure, preventing siphonage and ensuring harmful sewer odors stay inside the drainage system.
